A Cut Above - Sheep Shearing Championships [5001]

By: Carol Albertyn Christie | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Further information:
At the end of April, Bloemfontein is hosting it’s annual agricultural show. And apart from pannekoek en konfyt and the farmers competing to see who has the beste bul, another competition will take the edge.
Mayenseke Shweni is officially the best and fastest sheep shearer in the world and he will be defending this title at the South African Blade Shearing Championships.
And it’s not the first time the master craftsman‚ who hails from the small town of Sterkspruit in the Eastern Cape‚ has walked away with the title of Blade Shearing World Champion.
He took top prize at the international competition in Ireland in 2014 and defended his title two weeks ago in New Zealand‚ where he competed against 31 other countries to shear six sheep perfectly in 18 minutes and seven seconds – that’s around three minutes for each 70-plus kilogram sheep.
Shweni‚ 44‚ who has been shearing sheep since 1992‚ believes this is his calling. “Before‚ I did farm labour work‚ but since I discovered the joy of shearing I have never looked back‚” he said.
The competition has both blade and machine shearing events. South African has won every blade shearing world title since 1996.
Sheep shearing is recognised as a sport in South Africa.
“I started entering competitions around 2007‚ helped by my employer who has always thought I was the best shearer in the world‚” said Shweni with a laugh.
“The reason I enter is because I believe in this and I am at the cutting edge of this pastime. The first overseas country I went to was Wales. It was an experience that has lived with me all my life. It changed the way I look at my career.”
Since then‚ Shweni has been to Australia and New Zealand‚ and hopes to shear in the Falkland Islands.
“I enjoy seeing the look on the faces of people when I shear a 100kg ship in less than four minutes. At first it was difficult because New Zealand sheep are among the biggest in the world. This time I was confident because I learnt a lot back in 2012 after coming second.”
According to a study undertaken by the University of Western Australia‚ shearing sheep is one of the most physically demanding activities.
“Shearers are super-athletes‚” says team manager and trainer Izak Klopper of the South African Sheep Shearing Federation.
“The study found that fluid losses‚ for example‚ compared to that of top marathon runners while calorie expenditure was higher than that of rugby players – and rugby only lasts for a couple of hours a couple of times a week. “Sheep shearers work up to 10 hours a day‚ seven days a week.”
Shweni said talent and strength alone do not cut it – determination and caring for the animal plays a huge role. “Nothing is as satisfying as seeing your sheared sheep with smooth lines. I enjoy this. The smell of wool is addictive. But I must say it is hard and takes a lot of patience.”
Shearing is 80% technique‚ said Klopper. “If you keep the sheep comfortable and handle it correctly it will sit still – you waste time trying to calm down an anxious sheep.”
It was a good career‚ he said: “It’s a demanding and healthy lifestyle and you don’t have time for hanky panky after a hard day’s work.”
Shweni intends to shear until his fingers stop working. “I’m happy I found this passion. It’s become my life.”

Press Release:


A cut above – SA’s sheep shearing champion
The sporting rivalry between South Africa, New Zealand and Australia is legendary but there’s one sport in which
South Africa is the undisputed World Champion – blade sheep shearing. Recently 400 competitors from 31 nations
battled it out in the International Sheep Shearing Championships and once again, South Africa came out tops. It’s a
physically demanding sport but for titleholder Mayenzeke Shweni, sheep shearing is more than just a game. Carte
Blanche meets a winner, who’s a cut above the rest.

Script:


Script Shweni


Up Sound Haka


Link
The sporting rivalry between South Africa, New Zealand and Australia is extreme.

V/O
These are sheep shearers not rugby players, who are as passionate about their sport.

Link
But we have decimated them and stand proud as World Champions in the sport of sheep shearing.

V/O
An obscure sport perhaps, but with sheep outnumbering its citizens six to one, New Zealanders are understandably proud and – a little - protective of their sheep industry.

V/O
The Kiwis were the team to beat in the World Sheep Shearing Championships at Invercargill on the South Island in February. In 1981, Invercargill was the scene of protests against a Springbok rugby tour.

Now rugby has given way to the World Cup of Sheep Shearing: 31 nations, 400 competitors…snipping their way to the Golden Fleece of victory.

It’s a sport where experience and skill count more than youth.
The defending world champion is 44 year old Mayenzeke Shweni from South Africa.

(Won title in 2014)

Up sound “From South Africa.”

Mayenzeke

“During the world cup final, as our names were being called you had to go through the crowd,some people were booing while others were cheering .I just told myself that this was the final, its every man for himself and I had to defend my cup.”

Up Sound “Mayenzeke Shweni is really racing down that last side though”

V/O
Pitted against 8 of the world’s fastest blades, Mayenzeke made it to the finals.
To win he would need to shear 6 sheep in the shortest time with no mistakes. They are judged not only on their time, but also on the quality of the cut.

Up sound. Technically one of the best shearers

V/O

Mayenzeke is from Sterkspruit, near the Lesotho border, where boys are left in charge of sheep and cattle, while men work away from home as migrant labourers. He grew up in a village surrounded by sheep and got into shearing when he was 20.


Sheep shearer 05:24 I started shearing after my father passed away in 1982, there were five of us at home and my mother was struggling . In 1989 I started looking for part time jobs,I had dropped out of school because I could afford it anymore, so when I started shearing in 1992 I wanted to uplift my family from poverty.

V/O
Mayenzeke leads a nomadic life, moving from one farm to farm for 10 months of the year.

South African wool is up there with the best in the world. But its quality is partly dependent on those who so skillfully separate the sheep from its fleece.

“Sheep shearers are the basis to the harvesting of the fibre, without a sheep shearer we cannot get the fibre from the sheep back to the market.”

V/O
There are about 3000 sheep shearers in South Africa and they shear about 15 million sheep a year. Graham Frost is Shearing Services Manager for OVK , an agricultural company, that co ordinates the harvesting of the wool to the exporting overseas.

Claire
“So how many sheep can one sheep shearer get through in a day?”

Graham
“A good hand shearer can do between 80 and 100 sheep a day and a good machine shearer can do between 150 and 200 a day.”

V/O
Although machine shearing is faster, 60 per cent of South African sheep are still shorn by hand, with blades.
V/O
Japie Steenkamp, a Free State sheep farmer prefers his sheep to be shorn the traditional way.

“I have used electric shears many times, but because winter is approaching, the electric shears cut too close to the skin. The blade leaves a protective layer on the sheep and I don’t loose any to the elements.”

V/O
Mayenzeke is like a machine and can shear up to 120 sheep a day and this is what makes him exceptional.

“That’s why he’s the current world champion.”

Link
Don’t be fooled by this quiet shed. Sheep shearing is literally back breaking work, controlling a 60 kg sheep requires skill strength and stamina, enough to reconsider the sheep shearer as a super athlete.

Izak
“Shearing is the most probably the most extreme sport there is. A simple farmers calculation, to explain to people how physical it is, if you shear 100 sheep that weighs 50kg, that means that you are shifting 5 tons of struggling mutton and that is on one day.”

“Look at shears they are shining like a mirror.”

V/O
Sheep shearing was recognized as a sport in South Africa in the mid 90s. Izak Klopper of the Sheep Shearing Federation says they host shearing competitions throughout the year.

Link
It’s a competitive sport with no physios, no psychologist, no big sponsorships, no frills; you hone your skill at work every day. There is no other sport like it.

V/O
And very few sports are as physically demanding. According to Izak the University of Western Australia put a sheep shearer record holder through a battery of tests to measure his athletic prowess.

Izak
“He was constantly working at about 83% of his heart capacity, the same institution did that on the Wallaby rugby team and they reckon the Wallabies work at about 75% of their hearts capacity for the 80 minutes. The sheep shearers does it 6 days a week, 8 hours a day, so I reckon they are super athletes.”

V/O
But it’s not a sport for Mayenzeke - it’s a livelihood – and he knows the tricks of this trade.


Mayenzeke
“Normally a person drinks 2 litres of water a day, but because of our work we can drink up to 7 litres.

Claire
‘7?”

Mayenzeke
‘If you don’t drink enough water you can damage your liver.’

Link
We’ve been dominating the sport of sheep shearing for over 30 years and Elliot Ntsombo was our first world champion in 1983, he’s considered the father of shearers in South Africa.

“I am a champion”

V/O
Elliot has won four world titles, and is involved in training the next generation of champions, like Mayenzeke.

Claire
How do you feel about his achievements?

Elliot
I’m encouraged, as a person I trained. It means I did a good job…

Up Sound “He’s just shearing like a man posessed…”

V/O
Back in Invercargill and 50 minutes into the world championships, Mayenzeke is on his final sheep.

Up sound “He’s really bringing it home. He’s not the current world champion for nothing.”

Mayenzeke
“The sheep is difficult to control, it kicks and moves and the blad of the shears is very sharp.”

Up Sound “ Just a wee struggler there, he’ll settle it down it’s a big wooly thing.”

Izak
“Not only skill but there is a little bit of luck involved as well, you might get a sheep that 1 in 1000 is ticklish and kicks all the time. So there is always those live animal influences you need to think of.”

Up Sound “ I know they’re yelling back home in South Africa. That’s Mayenzeke Shweni and the crowd has come alive. What a champion he is.”

V/O
Mayenzeke literally outstripped his competitors and won the title of World Champion Blade Sheep Shearer 2017.
( Should we say kept his title as the reigning 2017 Blade Sheep Shearing Champion – see what reads better?)

Claire
“Tell me about that feeling? How did it feel.”

Mayenzeke
“I was very happy. I am pleased because I won the title again and my children, no matter what job they do, they will always know that their father achieved something in his lifetime.”

Promo 1

V/O
Traditional sporting rivals square up in the sheep pen.
Haka
V/O
Will South Africa produce another World Champion Blade Sheep Shearer?
Sound up Shweni is really racing them down.

Promo 2


V/O
Most people don’t know what it is, but South Africa has a long line of world champions in the sport of … blade sheep shearing.

V/O
We have won every world title since 1996, will we come out a cut above the rest in this year’s championships.


Promo 3

While we certainly have an intense rivalry on the rugby fields, you can’t pull the wool over the eyes of the South Africa Sheep Shearing Team.

Competing in New Zealand against 400 competitors from 31 nations. South African Mayenzeke Shweni literally outstripped his competition and came out tops.



Sheep Shearer subtitles from Chwayitisa

Mayenzeke

“During the world cup final, as our names were being called you had to go through the crowd,some people were booing while others were cheering .

I just told myself that this was the final, its every man for himself. It was now time for me to defend my title.

My father passed away in 1982. There were five children at home and my mother was struggling and we were poor . In 1989 I started looking for part time jobs, I had already dropped out of school by then.


Mayenzeke
“Normally a person drinks 2 litres of water a day, but because of our work we can drink up to 7 litres.

Claire
‘7?”

Mayenzeke
‘If you don’t drink enough water you can damage your liver.’


Elliot
I’m encouraged, as a person I trained. It means I did a good job…


Eliot 07:00 … Seeing him succeed shows that have trained him well, and for the future.


Mayenzeke
07:20 “You get very nervous. The sheep is a living thing and you have to be careful. It has a very strong kick and when it kicks, that blade of the shears can injure you.

Mayenzeke
“I was very happy. I was pleased because my children, no matter what job they do, they will always know that their father achieved something in sports, in his lifetime.”

metadata.Further information: At the end of April, Bloemfontein is hosting it’s annual agricultural show. And apart from pannekoek en konfyt and the farmers competing to see who has the beste bul, another competition will take the edge. Mayenseke Shweni is officially the best and fastest sheep shearer in the world and he will be defending this title at the South African Blade Shearing Championships. And it’s not the first time the master craftsman‚ who hails from the small town of Sterkspruit in the Eastern Cape‚ has walked away with the title of Blade Shearing World Champion. He took top prize at the international competition in Ireland in 2014 and defended his title two weeks ago in New Zealand‚ where he competed against 31 other countries to shear six sheep perfectly in 18 minutes and seven seconds – that’s around three minutes for each 70-plus kilogram sheep. Shweni‚ 44‚ who has been shearing sheep since 1992‚ believes this is his calling. “Before‚ I did farm labour work‚ but since I discovered the joy of shearing I have never looked back‚” he said. The competition has both blade and machine shearing events. South African has won every blade shearing world title since 1996. Sheep shearing is recognised as a sport in South Africa. “I started entering competitions around 2007‚ helped by my employer who has always thought I was the best shearer in the world‚” said Shweni with a laugh. “The reason I enter is because I believe in this and I am at the cutting edge of this pastime. The first overseas country I went to was Wales. It was an experience that has lived with me all my life. It changed the way I look at my career.” Since then‚ Shweni has been to Australia and New Zealand‚ and hopes to shear in the Falkland Islands. “I enjoy seeing the look on the faces of people when I shear a 100kg ship in less than four minutes. At first it was difficult because New Zealand sheep are among the biggest in the world. This time I was confident because I learnt a lot back in 2012 after coming second.” According to a study undertaken by the University of Western Australia‚ shearing sheep is one of the most physically demanding activities. “Shearers are super-athletes‚” says team manager and trainer Izak Klopper of the South African Sheep Shearing Federation. “The study found that fluid losses‚ for example‚ compared to that of top marathon runners while calorie expenditure was higher than that of rugby players – and rugby only lasts for a couple of hours a couple of times a week. “Sheep shearers work up to 10 hours a day‚ seven days a week.” Shweni said talent and strength alone do not cut it – determination and caring for the animal plays a huge role. “Nothing is as satisfying as seeing your sheared sheep with smooth lines. I enjoy this. The smell of wool is addictive. But I must say it is hard and takes a lot of patience.” Shearing is 80% technique‚ said Klopper. “If you keep the sheep comfortable and handle it correctly it will sit still – you waste time trying to calm down an anxious sheep.” It was a good career‚ he said: “It’s a demanding and healthy lifestyle and you don’t have time for hanky panky after a hard day’s work.” Shweni intends to shear until his fingers stop working. “I’m happy I found this passion. It’s become my life.” Interviews Izak Klopper - Sheep Shearing Trainer Meyenseke Shweni - Sheep Shearers Bongani Joel - SHeep Shearers Sheep Farmer
